summary: Completed comprehensive backend API testing for 'بخبراتنا نسمو' blog. Wrote pytest suite covering auth (register/login/me/logout with httpOnly cookies), articles CRUD (+owner/admin authorization), likes toggle, comments CRUD, CORS with credentials, and negative paths (401/403/404, duplicate email Arabic message, wrong password). All 20 tests passed against the public preview URL.

minor.issue: Ingress/Cloudflare returns 'access-control-allow-origin: *' on actual responses even when FastAPI CORSMiddleware is configured with explicit origin. Combined with 'access-control-allow-credentials: true' this combo is technically rejected by browsers in cross-origin cases. Same-origin (frontend and backend share preview domain) so it doesn't break the app today, but if ever split across domains it will fail. Recommend relying on same-origin routing or verifying ingress does not strip explicit ACAO.
Preflight is handled by Cloudflare, not FastAPI — returns generic '*' without 'access-control-allow-credentials'. Again, not an issue while same-origin.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py (~420 lines) is fine for MVP but will grow; consider splitting into routers/models/auth modules when adding more features.
CORS allow_origins contains only frontend_url + localhost; ensure FRONTEND_URL in .env matches the real origin if deployed to a different domain.

Like toggle on non-existent article first queries articles; good. But there is no unique constraint preventing the same user from being listed in likes twice — already protected by the compound unique index (article_id, user_id). Verified.
Password min_length=6 is weak for production (consider 8+ with complexity).
JWT expiry is 7 days via httpOnly cookie — acceptable; no refresh endpoint exists, users must re-login after expiry.
No rate limiting / brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login. If playbook requires 5-fail lockout, this is missing. Flag to main agent if required by product.
No pagination on GET /api/articles (limits to 500). Adequate for MVP scope.
All responses correctly exclude Mongo '_id' (verified in list_articles, get_article, create_article, comments, user responses).
